subject: physics_2
question_text: What is the force on a charged particle of charge q moving with velocity v in a uniform magnetic field of induction B? When is it maximum?

mark_split.label: F = B q v sin θ

verification.note: The 1+1 mark split is INVENTED and is a CLAIM until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it. For this paper the two-book union check and the past-paper back-test are both STRUCTURALLY IMPOSSIBLE: the TSBIE Basic Learning Material on hand is first-year physics only, and the paper corpus holds only Paper-I papers. Physics hand-checked: F = Bqv sin θ (the Lorentz magnetic force, F = q(v × B)); maximum F = Bqv when v ⊥ B. Matches the book's answer.

recall_prompt: Say the steps you would write for this answer, in order. You can speak in English, in Telugu, or in both.
insider_note: The same two-part shape as the conductor question: formula with θ named, then the θ = 90° maximum.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: The force formula
steps.mark_note: F = B q v sin θ, with θ named
lines: The force on the moving charge is

lines.text: F = B q v sin θ

lines: where θ is the angle between the
velocity v and the field B.
In vector form, F = q (v × B).
steps.margin_note: First mark. The angle θ is between v and B — say so beside the formula.
steps.why: The magnetic force uses only the part of the motion at right angles to the field; a charge at rest, or moving along the field, feels no force.
common_mistakes: Forgetting sin θ and writing F = B q v for every direction.
Applying the formula to a charge at rest. With v = 0 the force is zero.

recall.must_convey: That the force is F = B q v sin θ, with θ between v and B.
accept: F equals B q v sin theta

steps.memory_tip: Charge, speed, field — q v B — then sin θ for the angle between v and B.

steps.label: When it is maximum
steps.mark_note: θ = 90° and Fₘₐₓ = B q v
lines: The force is maximum when θ = 90°, that
is, when v is perpendicular to B.
steps.margin_note: Second mark. Condition and value together: v ⊥ B, F = B q v.
steps.why: sin θ reaches 1 only at 90°, so the push is strongest when the charge crosses the field lines at right angles.
common_mistakes: Saying maximum when v is along B. Along the field, θ = 0° and the force is zero.
Giving θ = 90° without writing the maximum value B q v.

recall.must_convey: That the force is maximum when v is perpendicular to B, where F = B q v.
accept: maximum when v perpendicular to B
F max is B q v
reject: maximum when v is along B

steps.memory_tip: Cross the field lines squarely for the biggest push; run along them for none.
